Foundation types for OpenTasks. All other Phase 1 work depends on this.

- `Anchor` interface for feedback positioning

- `Issue` interface (extends BaseNode, type: 'issue', status required)

### `src/schema/edges.ts`

### `src/schema/storage.ts`

title: Define Storage interface
content:
# Define Storage Interface

Domain-driven storage interface following beads pattern.

## Deliverables

### `src/storage/interface.ts`

```typescript
interface Storage {
  // Nodes
  createNode(node: StoredNode, actor?: string): Promise<void>
  getNode(id: string): Promise<StoredNode | null>
  updateNode(id: string, updates: Partial<StoredNode>, actor?: string): Promise<void>
  deleteNode(id: string, actor?: string): Promise<void>
  queryNodes(filter: NodeFilter): Promise<StoredNode[]>
  
  // Edges
  createEdge(edge: Edge, actor?: string): Promise<void>
  getEdge(id: string): Promise<Edge | null>
  deleteEdge(id: string, actor?: string): Promise<void>
  getEdgesFrom(nodeId: string, type?: EdgeType): Promise<Edge[]>
  getEdgesTo(nodeId: string, type?: EdgeType): Promise<Edge[]>
  
  // Tags (join table operations)
  addTag(nodeId: string, tag: string, actor?: string): Promise<void>
  removeTag(nodeId: string, tag: string, actor?: string): Promise<void>
  getTags(nodeId: string): Promise<string[]>
  getTagsForNodes(nodeIds: string[]): Promise<Map<string, string[]>>
  getNodesByTag(tag: string): Promise<StoredNode[]>
  
  // Queries
  getReady(): Promise<StoredNode[]>
  
  // Transactions
  runInTransaction<T>(fn: (tx: Transaction) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>
  
  // Dirty tracking
  markDirty(nodeId: string): Promise<void>
  getDirtyNodes(): Promise<string[]>
  clearDirty(nodeIds: string[]): Promise<void>
  
  // Lifecycle
  close(): Promise<void>
}

interface Transaction {
  createNode(node: StoredNode, actor?: string): Promise<void>
  updateNode(id: string, updates: Partial<StoredNode>, actor?: string): Promise<void>
  createEdge(edge: Edge, actor?: string): Promise<void>
  addTag(nodeId: string, tag: string, actor?: string): Promise<void>
}

interface NodeFilter {
  type?: string | string[]
  status?: string | string[]
  tags?: string[]  // AND semantics
  parent_id?: string
  archived?: boolean
  search?: string
  limit?: number
  offset?: number
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Interface covers all operations from spec
- [ ] Transaction interface is subset of Storage
- [ ] NodeFilter supports all query patterns
- [ ] Types are strict (no `any`)

## References

- [[s-4l4m|Phase 1: Core Data Layer]]
- Beads: `references/beads/internal/storage/storage.go`

title: Implement JSONL Persister
content:
# Implement JSONL Persister

Git-friendly JSONL storage as source of truth.

## Deliverables

### `src/storage/jsonl.ts`

```typescript
interface JSONLPersisterConfig {
  path: string                  // e.g., ".opentasks/graph.jsonl"
  tombstonesPath?: string       // e.g., ".opentasks/tombstones.jsonl"
  atomicWrite?: boolean         // default: true
}

class JSONLPersister {
  constructor(config: JSONLPersisterConfig)
  
  // Load entire graph
  async load(): Promise<{ nodes: StoredNode[]; edges: Edge[] }>
  
  // Save entire graph (atomic write)
  async save(nodes: StoredNode[], edges: Edge[]): Promise<void>
  
  // Append single entry (for incremental writes)
  async append(entry: StoredNode | Edge): Promise<void>
  
  // Watch for external changes
  watch(callback: () => void): () => void  // returns unsubscribe
  
  // Check if file exists
  async exists(): Promise<boolean>
}
```

### Helper: `src/storage/atomic-write.ts`

```typescript
async function atomicWrite(path: string, content: string): Promise<void>
```

## Implementation Notes

- Use `fs.watch()` or `chokidar` for file watching
- Atomic write: write to temp file, then rename
- Temp file naming: `${path}.${process.pid}.tmp`
- Parse JSONL line-by-line (handle large files)
- Separate nodes from edges by checking `from_id` presence or id prefix

## File Format

```jsonl
{"id":"s-a2b3","uuid":"...","type":"spec","title":"...","tags":["auth"],...}
{"id":"i-x7k9","uuid":"...","type":"issue","title":"...","status":"open",...}
{"id":"x-r8s9","uuid":"...","from_id":"i-x7k9","to_id":"s-a2b3","type":"implements",...}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `load()` parses JSONL correctly, separates nodes/edges
- [ ] `save()` uses atomic write (temp + rename)
- [ ] `append()` adds single line without rewriting file
- [ ] `watch()` detects external file changes
- [ ] Handles empty/missing file gracefully
- [ ] Preserves unknown fields (permissive)

## References

- [[s-4l4m|Phase 1: Core Data Layer]]
- Beads: `references/beads/internal/export/`

# Implement SQLite Persister

Fast query cache with better-sqlite3.

## Deliverables

### `src/storage/sqlite.ts`

```typescript
interface SQLitePersisterConfig {
  path: string                  // e.g., ".opentasks/cache.db"
  walMode?: boolean             // default: true
}

class SQLitePersister implements Storage {
  constructor(config: SQLitePersisterConfig)
  
  // Initialize database (create tables if needed)
  async initialize(): Promise<void>
  
  // Rebuild from JSONL (full import)
  async rebuildFromJsonl(jsonlPath: string): Promise<void>
  
  // All Storage interface methods...
}
```

### `src/storage/sqlite-schema.ts`

SQL schema as string constants for table creation.

## Schema

```sql
-- Nodes table
CREATE TABLE nodes (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  uuid TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  type TEXT NOT NULL,
  title TEXT NOT NULL,
  content TEXT,
  content_hash TEXT,
  status TEXT,
  priority INTEGER,
  assignee TEXT,
  parent_id TEXT,
  source TEXT,
  archived INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  target_id TEXT,
  feedback_type TEXT,
  uri TEXT,
  materialized INTEGER,
  FOREIGN KEY (parent_id) REFERENCES nodes(id)
);

-- Tags join table
CREATE TABLE node_tags (
  node_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  tag TEXT NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (node_id, tag),
  FOREIGN KEY (node_id) REFERENCES nodes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

-- Edges table
CREATE TABLE edges (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  uuid TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  from_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  to_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  type TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_by TEXT,
  source TEXT
);

-- Indexes
CREATE INDEX idx_nodes_type ON nodes(type);
CREATE INDEX idx_nodes_status ON nodes(status);
CREATE INDEX idx_nodes_parent ON nodes(parent_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_nodes_archived ON nodes(archived);
CREATE INDEX idx_node_tags_tag ON node_tags(tag);
CREATE INDEX idx_edges_from ON edges(from_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_edges_to ON edges(to_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_edges_type ON edges(type);

-- Ready issues view
CREATE VIEW ready_issues AS
SELECT n.* FROM nodes n
WHERE n.type = 'issue'
  AND n.status = 'open'
  AND n.archived = 0
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM edges e
    JOIN nodes blocker ON e.from_id = blocker.id
    WHERE e.to_id = n.id
      AND e.type = 'blocks'
      AND blocker.status != 'closed'
      AND blocker.archived = 0
  );

-- Dirty tracking
CREATE TABLE dirty_nodes (
  node_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  marked_at TEXT NOT NULL
);

-- Export hashes
CREATE TABLE export_hashes (
  node_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  content_hash TEXT NOT NULL
);
```

## Dependencies

Add to package.json:
```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "better-sqlite3": "^11.0.0"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@types/better-sqlite3": "^7.6.0"
  }
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `initialize()` creates all tables and indexes
- [ ] `rebuildFromJsonl()` imports full graph from JSONL
- [ ] Tag operations use join table correctly
- [ ] `getReady()` uses the view, returns correct issues
- [ ] `queryNodes()` builds correct WHERE clauses
- [ ] `runInTransaction()` properly commits/rollbacks
- [ ] Dirty tracking works (mark, get, clear)
- [ ] WAL mode enabled by default

## References

- [[s-4l4m|Phase 1: Core Data Layer]]
- Beads: `references/beads/internal/storage/sqlite/`

feedback.content:
## SQLite Persister Implementation Complete

### Requirements Met
- ✅ `initialize()` creates all tables and indexes
- ✅ `rebuildFromJsonl()` imports full graph from JSONL with tags
- ✅ Tag operations use join table correctly
- ✅ `getReady()` uses the view, returns correct issues
- ✅ `queryNodes()` builds correct WHERE clauses with all filters
- ✅ `runInTransaction()` properly commits (sync wrapper for better-sqlite3)
- ✅ Dirty tracking works (mark, get, clear)
- ✅ WAL mode enabled by default

### Design Decisions
- **Sync wrapper for transactions**: better-sqlite3 is synchronous, so transactions collect operations and execute them in a batch sync transaction
- **Boolean fields**: Stored as 0/1 integers, converted on read/write
- **Tags in getNode**: Tags are fetched separately and attached to node on retrieval
- **Tag filtering in queries**: Uses AND semantics (all tags must match)

- `src/storage/sqlite-schema.ts` - All SQL schema as string constants
- `src/storage/sqlite.ts` - Full `SQLitePersister` class implementing `Storage` interface

title: Extract DebouncedFlusher from SyncManager
content:
## Summary
Refactor the existing SyncManager to extract a core `DebouncedFlusher` utility that handles timing without coupling to Storage.

## Background
Current SyncManager is coupled to Storage (for `markDirty` persistence). The daemon FlushManager needs the same debounce/maxDelay timing logic but with different flush behavior. Extracting a shared utility avoids duplication.

## Requirements

### DebouncedFlusher Interface
```typescript
interface DebouncedFlusher {
  /** Mark that changes exist */
  markDirty(): void
  
  /** Schedule debounced flush */
  schedule(): void
  
  /** Force immediate flush */
  flush(): Promise<void>
  
  /** Cancel pending flush */
  cancel(): void
  
  /** Check if flush pending */
  hasPending(): boolean
}

function createDebouncedFlusher(
  config: { debounceMs: number; maxDelayMs: number },
  onFlush: () => Promise<void>
): DebouncedFlusher
```

### Changes
1. Create `src/graph/debounce.ts` with `createDebouncedFlusher`
2. Refactor `src/graph/sync.ts` to compose `DebouncedFlusher`
3. Keep SyncManager's existing interface for backwards compatibility
4. Update exports in `src/graph/index.ts`
5. Ensure all existing tests still pass

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] DebouncedFlusher works standalone (no Storage dependency)
- [ ] SyncManager composes DebouncedFlusher internally
- [ ] Existing SyncManager tests pass unchanged
- [ ] New unit tests for DebouncedFlusher in isolation
- [ ] Debounce and maxDelay behavior preserved

## References
- [[s-9r97|Phase 3: Daemon & IPC]] - Section 3.1

title: Implement lock file operations
content:
## Summary
Implement lock file operations for daemon exclusivity - only one daemon per `.opentasks/` location.

## Requirements

### Lock File Format
```typescript
// .opentasks/daemon.lock
interface DaemonLock {
  pid: number
  parentPid: number
  version: string
  startedAt: string       // ISO timestamp
  socketPath: string
  databasePath: string
}
```

### Lock Manager Interface
```typescript
interface LockManager {
  /** Attempt to acquire lock, throws if already held */
  acquire(metadata: Omit<DaemonLock, 'pid' | 'parentPid' | 'startedAt'>): Promise<void>
  
  /** Release the lock */
  release(): Promise<void>
  
  /** Check if lock is held by a live process */
  isHeld(): Promise<boolean>
  
  /** Read lock file contents (if exists) */
  read(): Promise<DaemonLock | null>
}
```

### Implementation Details
1. Use `flock` for exclusive locking (via `fs-ext` or `proper-lockfile` package)
2. Lock file at `.opentasks/daemon.lock`
3. Write JSON contents after acquiring flock
4. Check if PID in lock file is alive before declaring stale
5. Handle stale locks (process died without cleanup)

### File Structure
- `src/daemon/lock.ts` - Lock manager implementation
- `src/daemon/__tests__/lock.test.ts` - Unit tests

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Can acquire lock when none exists
- [ ] Can detect existing lock held by live process
- [ ] Can steal stale lock (process dead)
- [ ] Lock contents include all metadata
- [ ] Clean release removes lock file
- [ ] Concurrent acquire attempts handled correctly

## References
- [[s-9r97|Phase 3: Daemon & IPC]] - Section 3.2

feedback.content:
**Implemented lock file operations**

Created `src/daemon/lock.ts` with `LockManager`:
- Uses `proper-lockfile` package for cross-platform file locking
- Lock file at `.opentasks/daemon.lock` contains PID, version, socket path, database path
- Detects stale locks (process died) and allows stealing them
- Prevents concurrent daemon instances per location
- 18 unit tests covering acquire, release, isHeld, read, concurrent access

Created `src/daemon/types.ts` with shared daemon types:
- `DaemonLock`, `LockMetadata`
- `DaemonRegistry`, `DaemonEntry` (for registry)
- `DaemonStatus`, `DaemonState`
- `DaemonError` class with typed error codes

Module exports via `src/daemon/index.ts`.

title: Implement global daemon registry
content:
## Summary
Implement the global registry at `~/.opentasks/registry.json` that tracks all running daemons.

## Requirements

### Auto-initialization
- Create `~/.opentasks/` directory if missing when first daemon registers
- Create `registry.json` with initial structure
- Do NOT initialize as full OpenTasks location (no graph.jsonl, cache.db)

### Registry Format
```typescript
interface DaemonRegistry {
  version: string
  daemons: DaemonEntry[]
}

interface DaemonEntry {
  /** Absolute path to .opentasks/ directory */
  locationPath: string
  
  /** Socket path for IPC */
  socketPath: string
  
  /** Process ID */
  pid: number
  
  /** OpenTasks version */
  version: string
  
  /** When daemon started */
  startedAt: string
  
  /** Last activity timestamp */
  lastActivity: string
}
```

### Registry Manager Interface
```typescript
interface RegistryManager {
  /** Register daemon on startup */
  register(entry: DaemonEntry): Promise<void>
  
  /** Unregister daemon on shutdown */
  unregister(locationPath: string): Promise<void>
  
  /** Find daemon for a location */
  find(locationPath: string): Promise<DaemonEntry | null>
  
  /** List all registered daemons */
  list(): Promise<DaemonEntry[]>
  
  /** Remove stale entries (dead PIDs) */
  cleanup(): Promise<number>
}
```

### Implementation Details
1. File-based JSON storage with atomic writes
2. Use file locking when modifying registry
3. Cleanup checks PIDs with `process.kill(pid, 0)`
4. Handle concurrent access from multiple daemons

### File Structure
- `src/daemon/registry.ts` - Registry manager implementation
- `src/daemon/__tests__/registry.test.ts` - Unit tests

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Auto-creates ~/.opentasks/ on first register
- [ ] Registry persists across process restarts
- [ ] Can register/unregister daemons
- [ ] Find returns correct daemon for location
- [ ] Cleanup removes dead daemon entries
- [ ] Concurrent modifications handled safely

## References
- [[s-9r97|Phase 3: Daemon & IPC]] - Section 3.3

feedback.content:
**Implemented global daemon registry**

Created `src/daemon/registry.ts` with `RegistryManager`:
- Registry at `~/.opentasks/registry.json` (customizable path for testing)
- Auto-creates directory on first register (does NOT create full OpenTasks location)
- File locking with `proper-lockfile` for concurrent access safety
- Atomic writes via temp file + rename
- 21 unit tests covering register, unregister, find, list, cleanup, persistence

Features:
- `register(entry)` - Add/replace daemon entry
- `unregister(locationPath)` - Remove daemon entry  
- `find(locationPath)` - Find daemon, returns null if PID dead
- `list()` - List all entries (including dead PIDs)
- `cleanup()` - Remove entries with dead PIDs

Helper exported: `getGlobalRegistryPath()` returns `~/.opentasks/registry.json`

title: Implement IPC server with lifecycle methods
content:
## Summary
Implement the IPC server using Unix domain sockets with JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol and lifecycle methods.

## Requirements

### Transport
- Unix domain socket: `.opentasks/daemon.sock`
- Line-based JSON-RPC 2.0 (newline-delimited)

### Protocol Format
```
Request:  {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping","params":{}}\\n
Response: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"pong":true}}\\n
Error:    {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"error":{"code":-32600,"message":"..."}}\\n
```

### IPC Server Interface
```typescript
interface IPCServer {
  /** Start listening on socket */
  start(): Promise<void>
  
  /** Stop accepting connections */
  stop(): Promise<void>
  
  /** Register method handler */
  handle<P, R>(method: string, handler: (params: P) => Promise<R>): void
}

interface IPCRequest {
  jsonrpc: '2.0'
  id: string | number
  method: string
  params?: unknown
}

interface IPCResponse {
  jsonrpc: '2.0'
  id: string | number
  result?: unknown
  error?: {
    code: number
    message: string
    data?: unknown
  }
}
```

### Phase 3a Lifecycle Methods
| Method | Description | Response |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| `ping` | Health check | `{pong: true}` |
| `health` | Detailed health status | `{status, uptime, memory, ...}` |
| `status` | Daemon status and stats | `{state, connectionCount, ...}` |
| `shutdown` | Graceful shutdown | `{success: true}` |

### Implementation Details
1. Use Node.js `net` module for Unix sockets
2. Parse incoming lines as JSON-RPC requests
3. Route to registered handlers by method name
4. Handle malformed requests with JSON-RPC errors
5. Support multiple concurrent connections

### Error Codes (JSON-RPC standard)
- `-32700` Parse error
- `-32600` Invalid request
- `-32601` Method not found
- `-32602` Invalid params
- `-32603` Internal error

### File Structure
- `src/daemon/ipc.ts` - IPC server implementation
- `src/daemon/methods/lifecycle.ts` - Lifecycle method handlers
- `src/daemon/__tests__/ipc.test.ts` - Unit tests

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Server starts on Unix socket
- [ ] Handles JSON-RPC 2.0 requests
- [ ] Routes to registered handlers
- [ ] Returns proper error responses
- [ ] Lifecycle methods work (ping, health, status, shutdown)
- [ ] Multiple concurrent connections supported
- [ ] Clean shutdown closes all connections

## References
- [[s-9r97|Phase 3: Daemon & IPC]] - Section 3.4

feedback.content:
**Implemented IPC server with lifecycle methods**

Created `src/daemon/ipc.ts` with `IPCServer`:
- Unix domain socket using Node.js `net` module
- Line-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol
- Method handler registration with `handle(method, handler)`
- Connection tracking with `getConnectionCount()`
- Standard JSON-RPC error codes (parse error, method not found, invalid params, internal error)
- 23 unit tests covering server, client, lifecycle methods

Also created `IPCClient` for testing and internal use.

Created `src/daemon/methods/lifecycle.ts` with handlers:
- `ping` - Returns `{pong: true}`
- `health` - Returns status, uptime, memory usage, version
- `status` - Returns full DaemonStatus
- `shutdown` - Triggers graceful shutdown (via setImmediate to send response first)

All methods tested end-to-end through IPC.

title: Implement file watcher for external changes
content:
## Summary
Implement file watching to detect external changes to watched files and reload state.

## Requirements

### Watched Files
1. `graph.jsonl` - Source of truth, detect external edits
2. `specs/*.md` - Markdown files (if expansion enabled)
3. `issues/*.md` - Markdown files (if expansion enabled)
4. `config.json` - Configuration changes

### FileWatcher Interface
```typescript
interface FileWatcher {
  /** Start watching */
  start(): void
  
  /** Stop watching */
  stop(): void
  
  /** Pause during internal writes */
  pause(): void
  
  /** Resume after internal writes */
  resume(): void
}
```

### Change Detection Flow
```
External edit detected:
1. Pause flush manager (prevent write conflicts)
2. Reload affected data from file
3. Merge with in-memory state (or replace if conflict)
4. Mark as dirty for next flush cycle
5. Resume flush manager
```

### Implementation Details
1. Use `chokidar` or Node.js `fs.watch`/`fs.watchFile`
2. Debounce rapid file changes (editors may write multiple times)
3. Distinguish internal writes (paused) from external writes
4. Handle file deletion gracefully
5. Watch for new markdown files in specs/issues directories

### File Structure
- `src/daemon/watcher.ts` - File watcher implementation
- `src/daemon/__tests__/watcher.test.ts` - Unit tests

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Detects changes to graph.jsonl
- [ ] Detects changes to markdown files
- [ ] Detects changes to config.json
- [ ] Pause/resume prevents detecting own writes
- [ ] Debounces rapid changes
- [ ] Triggers reload on external change
- [ ] Handles file deletion

## References
- [[s-9r97|Phase 3: Daemon & IPC]] - Section 3.5

feedback.content:
**Implemented file watcher**

Created `src/daemon/watcher.ts` with `createFileWatcher`:
- Uses `chokidar` for cross-platform file watching
- Watches: graph.jsonl, config.json, specs/*.md, issues/*.md
- Debounces rapid changes (configurable delay)
- Pause/resume to ignore internal writes
- File categorization (graph, spec, issue, config)
- 17 unit tests covering detection, pause/resume, debouncing, multiple handlers

Features:
- `start()` / `stop()` - Control watching
- `pause()` / `resume()` - Ignore events during internal writes
- `onchange(handler)` - Register change handlers
- Change events include type (add/change/unlink), path, and category

Optional `watchMarkdown` config to disable markdown file watching.

title: Implement basic daemon lifecycle
content:
## Summary
Implement the core daemon lifecycle - start and stop sequences with proper coordination.

## Requirements

### Startup Sequence
```
1. Check for existing daemon (lock file exists + process alive)
2. If existing daemon running → return socket path (or error)
3. Acquire exclusive flock on .opentasks/daemon.lock
4. Write lock file contents (PID, metadata)
5. Initialize GraphStore (loads from JSONL → SQLite)
6. Start IPC server on .opentasks/daemon.sock
7. Register in global registry (~/.opentasks/registry.json)
8. Start file watchers
9. Start flush manager
10. Ready to accept connections
```

### Shutdown Sequence
```
1. Stop accepting new connections
2. Finish in-flight requests (2s timeout)
3. Stop file watchers
4. Final flush to JSONL
5. Unregister from global registry
6. Close IPC server
7. Remove socket file
8. Release lock file
```

### Signal Handling
- SIGTERM → graceful shutdown
- SIGINT (Ctrl+C) → graceful shutdown

### Daemon Interface
```typescript
interface Daemon {
  /** Start the daemon */
  start(): Promise<void>
  
  /** Stop the daemon gracefully */
  stop(): Promise<void>
  
  /** Get daemon status */
  getStatus(): DaemonStatus
  
  /** Socket path for IPC */
  socketPath: string
}

interface DaemonStatus {
  state: 'starting' | 'running' | 'stopping' | 'stopped'
  startedAt: string
  pid: number
  socketPath: string
  pendingFlush: boolean
  connectionCount: number
}
```

### File Structure
- `src/daemon/lifecycle.ts` - Daemon implementation
- `src/daemon/__tests__/lifecycle.test.ts` - Unit tests

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Daemon starts and acquires lock
- [ ] Daemon registers in global registry
- [ ] Daemon handles SIGTERM/SIGINT gracefully
- [ ] Shutdown completes within timeout
- [ ] Resources cleaned up on stop (socket, lock)
- [ ] Can detect already-running daemon

## Dependencies
- Lock file operations [[i-xxx]] (will link)
- Global registry [[i-xxx]] (will link)

## References
- [[s-9r97|Phase 3: Daemon & IPC]] - Section 3.2

feedback.content:
**Implemented basic daemon lifecycle**

Created `src/daemon/lifecycle.ts` with `createDaemon`:
- Start sequence: check existing → acquire lock → remove stale socket → register in registry → setup signal handlers
- Stop sequence: remove signal handlers → unregister → remove socket → release lock
- Signal handling: SIGTERM and SIGINT trigger graceful shutdown
- Shutdown timeout: configurable (default 2s)
- 21 unit tests covering start, stop, status, restart, error handling

Exported helpers:
- `checkExistingDaemon(locationPath)` - Check if daemon already running
- `createDaemon(config)` - Create daemon instance

State machine: stopped → starting → running → stopping → stopped

title: Implement daemon flush manager
content:
## Summary
Implement the daemon-specific flush manager that wraps DebouncedFlusher with coordination for file watching.

## Requirements

### DaemonFlushManager Interface
```typescript
interface DaemonFlushManager {
  /** Mark node as dirty */
  markDirty(nodeId: string): void
  
  /** Schedule debounced flush */
  schedule(): void
  
  /** Force immediate flush */
  flush(): Promise<void>
  
  /** Pause flushing (for file watcher) */
  pause(): void
  
  /** Resume flushing */
  resume(): void
  
  /** Final flush on shutdown */
  finalFlush(): Promise<void>
}
```

### Implementation Details
1. Compose `DebouncedFlusher` from issue 1
2. Track dirty nodes (not just boolean dirty flag)
3. Pause/resume to coordinate with file watcher
4. Final flush ensures all changes written before shutdown
5. Integrates with GraphStore for actual persistence

### Flush Operation
```
1. Get list of dirty node IDs
2. For each dirty node:
   a. Read current state from SQLite
   b. Append to JSONL
3. Clear dirty tracking
4. If file watcher detected conflicts, merge first
```

### File Structure
- `src/daemon/flush.ts` - Flush manager implementation
- `src/daemon/__tests__/flush.test.ts` - Unit tests

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Uses DebouncedFlusher for timing
- [ ] Tracks dirty nodes by ID
- [ ] Pause/resume work correctly
- [ ] Final flush writes all pending changes
- [ ] Coordinates with file watcher (no conflicts)
- [ ] Debounce and maxDelay behavior correct

## Dependencies
- [[i-xxx]] DebouncedFlusher (will link)

## References
- [[s-9r97|Phase 3: Daemon & IPC]] - Section 3.6

feedback.content:
**Implemented daemon flush manager**

Created `src/daemon/flush.ts` with `createDaemonFlushManager`:
- Composes `DebouncedFlusher` for timing logic
- Tracks dirty nodes by ID (deduplication)
- Pause/resume for file watcher coordination
- `finalFlush()` ignores pause state for shutdown
- 28 unit tests covering all functionality

Features:
- `markDirty(nodeId)` - Track node as dirty
- `schedule()` - Schedule debounced flush
- `flush()` - Force immediate flush
- `pause()` / `resume()` - Coordinate with file watcher
- `finalFlush()` - Shutdown flush (ignores pause)
- `getDirtyNodes()` - Get list of dirty node IDs
- `hasPendingChanges()` - Check if flush needed

Default config: 5s debounce, 30s max delay.
